name: Mini-cut

lead: A mini-cut is a brief, aggressive cutting phase, often lasting a few weeks, used to lose a limited amount of fat before returning to maintenance or a bulk.
The term is common in bodybuilding and lifting communities. Few sources describe it in detail, and no clinical studies were found.

paras: Calories are cut more sharply than in a regular cut for a short period. A Grokipedia summary says the early weight lost is mostly water and glycogen, with about 1 to 2 percent body fat reduction.
The same summary lists a higher chance of muscle loss, fatigue and metabolic slowdown, and recommends more gradual rates for most people. Aggressive deficits are described as riskier.

lead: A mini-cut is a short, aggressive cutting phase in which a lifter eats well below maintenance for a few weeks to reduce body fat, usually between longer bulking phases.[1] A Grokipedia summary describes them as lasting about 2 to 6 weeks.[1]

The same source says mini-cuts typically produce a few pounds of weight loss, much of it water and glycogen, and about 1 to 2 percent body fat reduction, with higher risks of muscle loss, fatigue and metabolic slowdown than a gradual cut.[1] Wikipedia notes that larger deficits cause faster weight loss but a greater risk of losing muscle.[2]
No clinical studies on mini-cuts were found.

paras: Cutting is eating in a net negative energy balance to lose fat while preserving muscle.[2] A mini-cut compresses this into a shorter, steeper deficit.[1]

A Grokipedia summary reports most early weight lost is water and glycogen, with modest fat reduction, and cites greater risks of muscle loss, fatigue and metabolic slowdown.[1] It recommends more gradual loss for most people.[1]
